_comment: Gate TIERS. Every enumerable test is a gate and every gate is counted; the
tier says what KIND of gate it is, so the board can render an edge-case
square differently from a core-requirement square and a scorecard can quote
a core-only pass bar without hiding the edge gates from the denominator.
A tier is NOT a way to make a gate optional. `total` stays the true count of
everything enumerable (invariant I-1); tiers only partition it.
RULE: a test file with a path segment named `edge` is tier `edge`. Anything
else is `default`. Deliberately a path convention rather than a per-test
list — a list drifts silently the moment a test is renamed, and a silently
wrong tier is the same class of defect as a silently wrong count.
Absent or unreadable, every gate is `default` — never unlabelled.

rules.why: boundary and degenerate-input gates: real requirements, but not the core capability the benchmark headline measures
